### Upstream Dolphin PR [#14736](https://github.com/dolphin-emu/dolphin/pull/14736)
**Title:** Auto assign wii controllers in netplay
**Author:** [@tom-pratt](https://github.com/tom-pratt)

#### PR Description
Just copy the gamecube logic and automatically assign players to the first empty slot.

More consistent with GameCube and helps Android hosts where there is no UI for managing controller mappings currently.

This is an unofficial community build, not affiliated with the Dolphin team.

eden-4301-0295dc5fff9b2977e753e7c126cc87.changelog:
Pull request build #[4301](https://git.eden-emu.dev/eden-emu/eden/pulls/4301)

Commit: [`0295dc5fff9b2977e753e7c126cc870abb07ee3f`](https://git.eden-emu.dev/eden-emu/eden/commit/0295dc5fff9b2977e753e7c126cc870abb07ee3f)

Merge base: [`0295dc5fff`](https://git.eden-emu.dev/eden-emu/eden/commit/0295dc5fff)
([Master Build](https://git.eden-emu.dev/eden-ci/master/releases?q=0295dc5fff&expanded=true))

## Changelog
This PR removes the artificial limit added for QCOM drivers based on a sampler budget limit (based on #3280 work), removes the ban on CustomBorderColor/BorderColorSwizzle for also QCOM driver, reduce the amount of combination required to created a sampler with custom border color/ color border swizzle; adds cases on R16 formats not able to swizzle on BGR565 formats; degrades samplers and color combinations when there's no color border swizzle available; fixes the srgb (LUT) values from legacy and now all the color variations are cached in the same key, instead of having 7 different handlers for them. In resume, rather than performance (due to the reduced amount of process on duplicated/ synced code on pipeline/texture cache), it's a graphica accuracy work that will improve image quality at the cost of almost 0 performance hit, rather than certain hitch if the color combination wasn't cached before. This applies to all platform.


# Packages

## Targets

Each build is optimized for a specific architecture and uses a specific compiler.

- **arm64-v8a**: For devices that use the armv8-a instruction set; e.g. Snapdragon X, all Android devices, and Apple Silicon Macs.
- **x86_64**: For devices that use the x86_64 instruction set; this is exclusively used by Intel and AMD CPUs and is only found on desktops.
- **v3**: For devices that use the x86_64-v3 instruction set or newer; this is found on Ryzen, Intel 4th Generation (Haswell), and newer.

### PGO

PGO builds usually perform ~10-30% better than standard builds, and are thus generally recommended for all users.

## Linux

Linux packages are distributed via AppImage.
[zsync](https://zsync.moria.org.uk/) files are provided for easier updating, such as via
[AM](https://github.com/ivan-hc/AM).

## Changelog
This PR removes the artificial limit added for QCOM drivers based on a sampler budget limit (based on #3280 work), removes the ban on CustomBorderColor/BorderColorSwizzle for also QCOM driver, reduce the amount of combination required to created a sampler with custom border color/ color border swizzle; adds cases on R16 formats not able to swizzle on BGR565 formats; degrades samplers and color combinations when there's no color border swizzle available; fixes the srgb (LUT) values from legacy and now all the color variations are cached in the same key, instead of having 7 different handlers for them. In resume, rather than performance (due to the reduced amount of process on duplicated/ synced code on pipeline/texture cache), it's a graphica accuracy work that will improve image quality at the cost of almost 0 performance hit, rather than certain hitch if the color combination wasn't cached before. This applies to all platform.

## Changelog
This PR removes the artificial limit added for QCOM drivers based on a sampler budget limit (based on #3280 work), removes the ban on CustomBorderColor/BorderColorSwizzle for also QCOM driver, reduce the amount of combination required to created a sampler with custom border color/ color border swizzle; adds cases on R16 formats not able to swizzle on BGR565 formats; degrades samplers and color combinations when there's no color border swizzle available; fixes the srgb (LUT) values from legacy and now all the color variations are cached in the same key, instead of having 7 different handlers for them. In resume, rather than performance (due to the reduced amount of process on duplicated/ synced code on pipeline/texture cache), it's a graphica accuracy work that will improve image quality at the cost of almost 0 performance hit, rather than certain hitch if the color combination wasn't cached before. This applies to all platform.

## Changelog
This PR removes the artificial limit added for QCOM drivers based on a sampler budget limit (based on #3280 work), removes the ban on CustomBorderColor/BorderColorSwizzle for also QCOM driver, reduce the amount of combination required to created a sampler with custom border color/ color border swizzle; adds cases on R16 formats not able to swizzle on BGR565 formats; degrades samplers and color combinations when there's no color border swizzle available; fixes the srgb (LUT) values from legacy and now all the color variations are cached in the same key, instead of having 7 different handlers for them. In resume, rather than performance (due to the reduced amount of process on duplicated/ synced code on pipeline/texture cache), it's a graphica accuracy work that will improve image quality at the cost of almost 0 performance hit, rather than certain hitch if the color combination wasn't cached before. This applies to all platform.


# Packages

## Targets

Each build is optimized for a specific architecture and uses a specific compiler.

- **arm64-v8a**: For devices that use the armv8-a instruction set; e.g. Snapdragon X, all Android devices, and Apple Silicon Macs.
- **x86_64**: For devices that use the x86_64 instruction set; this is exclusively used by Intel and AMD CPUs and is only found on desktops.
- **v3**: For devices that use the x86_64-v3 instruction set or newer; this is found on Ryzen, Intel 4th Generation (Haswell), and newer.

### PGO

PGO builds usually perform ~10-30% better than standard builds, and are thus generally recommended for all users.

## Changelog
This PR removes the artificial limit added for QCOM drivers based on a sampler budget limit (based on #3280 work), removes the ban on CustomBorderColor/BorderColorSwizzle for also QCOM driver, reduce the amount of combination required to created a sampler with custom border color/ color border swizzle; adds cases on R16 formats not able to swizzle on BGR565 formats; degrades samplers and color combinations when there's no color border swizzle available; fixes the srgb (LUT) values from legacy and now all the color variations are cached in the same key, instead of having 7 different handlers for them. In resume, rather than performance (due to the reduced amount of process on duplicated/ synced code on pipeline/texture cache), it's a graphica accuracy work that will improve image quality at the cost of almost 0 performance hit, rather than certain hitch if the color combination wasn't cached before. This applies to all platform.

## Changelog
This PR removes the artificial limit added for QCOM drivers based on a sampler budget limit (based on #3280 work), removes the ban on CustomBorderColor/BorderColorSwizzle for also QCOM driver, reduce the amount of combination required to created a sampler with custom border color/ color border swizzle; adds cases on R16 formats not able to swizzle on BGR565 formats; degrades samplers and color combinations when there's no color border swizzle available; fixes the srgb (LUT) values from legacy and now all the color variations are cached in the same key, instead of having 7 different handlers for them. In resume, rather than performance (due to the reduced amount of process on duplicated/ synced code on pipeline/texture cache), it's a graphica accuracy work that will improve image quality at the cost of almost 0 performance hit, rather than certain hitch if the color combination wasn't cached before. This applies to all platform.

## Changelog
This PR removes the artificial limit added for QCOM drivers based on a sampler budget limit (based on #3280 work), removes the ban on CustomBorderColor/BorderColorSwizzle for also QCOM driver, reduce the amount of combination required to created a sampler with custom border color/ color border swizzle; adds cases on R16 formats not able to swizzle on BGR565 formats; degrades samplers and color combinations when there's no color border swizzle available; fixes the srgb (LUT) values from legacy and now all the color variations are cached in the same key, instead of having 7 different handlers for them. In resume, rather than performance (due to the reduced amount of process on duplicated/ synced code on pipeline/texture cache), it's a graphica accuracy work that will improve image quality at the cost of almost 0 performance hit, rather than certain hitch if the color combination wasn't cached before. This applies to all platform.


# Packages

## Targets

Each build is optimized for a specific architecture and uses a specific compiler.

- **arm64-v8a**: For devices that use the armv8-a instruction set; e.g. Snapdragon X, all Android devices, and Apple Silicon Macs.
- **x86_64**: For devices that use the x86_64 instruction set; this is exclusively used by Intel and AMD CPUs and is only found on desktops.
- **v3**: For devices that use the x86_64-v3 instruction set or newer; this is found on Ryzen, Intel 4th Generation (Haswell), and newer.

## Changelog
This PR removes the artificial limit added for QCOM drivers based on a sampler budget limit (based on #3280 work), removes the ban on CustomBorderColor/BorderColorSwizzle for also QCOM driver, reduce the amount of combination required to created a sampler with custom border color/ color border swizzle; adds cases on R16 formats not able to swizzle on BGR565 formats; degrades samplers and color combinations when there's no color border swizzle available; fixes the srgb (LUT) values from legacy and now all the color variations are cached in the same key, instead of having 7 different handlers for them. In resume, rather than performance (due to the reduced amount of process on duplicated/ synced code on pipeline/texture cache), it's a graphica accuracy work that will improve image quality at the cost of almost 0 performance hit, rather than certain hitch if the color combination wasn't cached before. This applies to all platform.

# Packages

## Targets

Each build is optimized for a specific architecture and uses a specific compiler.

- **arm64-v8a**: For devices that use the armv8-a instruction set; e.g. Snapdragon X, all Android devices, and Apple Silicon Macs.
- **x86_64**: For devices that use the x86_64 instruction set; this is exclusively used by Intel and AMD CPUs and is only found on desktops.
- **v3**: For devices that use the x86_64-v3 instruction set or newer; this is found on Ryzen, Intel 4th Generation (Haswell), and newer.

### PGO

PGO builds usually perform ~10-30% better than standard builds, and are thus generally recommended for all users.

[zsync](https://zsync.moria.org.uk/) files are provided for easier updating, such as via

# Packages

## Targets

Each build is optimized for a specific architecture and uses a specific compiler.

- **arm64-v8a**: For devices that use the armv8-a instruction set; e.g. Snapdragon X, all Android devices, and Apple Silicon Macs.
- **x86_64**: For devices that use the x86_64 instruction set; this is exclusively used by Intel and AMD CPUs and is only found on desktops.
- **v3**: For devices that use the x86_64-v3 instruction set or newer; this is found on Ryzen, Intel 4th Generation (Haswell), and newer.

### PGO

PGO builds usually perform ~10-30% better than standard builds, and are thus generally recommended for all users.
